what_was_done: The property test's between-quotes position now always carries a character a quoted span refuses. The junk is drawn from the same alphabet as before (excluded characters plus single quote, U+0000 to U+001F, DEL), then one character drawn from the single quote and U+0000 to U+001F and U+007F is inserted at a random index of the draw, and the test asserts that precondition on inner (some character is a quote, below U+0020 or U+007F) before asserting refusal. The two wrong comments are corrected: the alphabet the junk draws from is no longer described as 'what a quoted span must refuse' (printable excluded characters are legal inside a quoted span, e.g. vsdd survey --flag value 'x$!'), and the in-branch comment no longer claims the junk itself may not sit inside a quoted span. The test now runs its 200 draws under six seeds in one body (20261124, 1, 2, 3, 42, 20261125), so no single lucky seed can keep a wrong construction green: reproduced first that the old construction, code unchanged, fails under seeds 1, 2, 3, 42 and 20261125 on clean calls ('x$!', 'x\<', 'x*', 'x*}', 'x<<') while seed 20261124 passes. Added the deterministic per-code-point test the finding asked for: test_every_control_character_is_refused_between_quotes asserts for every code point in U+0000 to U+001F and U+007F that vsdd survey 'a<c>b' is refused, both by caller._CALL_TEXT_RE alone and through caller.is_vsdd_call. caller.py needed no change (the quoted-span class was already right; only its pinning was weak), and the grammar passage in rewrite/spec/topics/caller-identity.md already states the rule, so neither was touched. Confirmation: in a scratch copy of the tree, widening _QUOTED to admit U+0001 alone failed both the property test (it approves 'vsdd survey --flag value 'x\x01!'' end to end) and the per-code-point test at code=1, and widening it to admit DEL failed the per-code-point test at code=0x7F - the property draw never had DEL as its sole refused character, which is exactly why the deterministic loop was added. Four-shell canary sweep re-run: 148 grammar-accepted texts (the 13-entry allowed table, 6 edge forms and 129 fuzzed texts with quoted metacharacters, blanks and non-ASCII), each filtered through _CALL_TEXT_RE alone and is_vsdd_call, ran under /bin/sh, /bin/bash 3.2.57, /bin/dash and /bin/zsh 5.9 as 592 runs; every run executed exactly the logging vsdd canary once with argv equal to the POSIX tokenization of the text and no hidden canary ever ran (zero failures); a negative control confirmed the harness detects the hidden run of a refused text ($(hid pwned)).
